stories.title: Alberta takes symbolic stand against federal hate crime law, says it silences speech
stories.summary: The UCP government is expected to invoke the sovereignty act in the legislature and table a motion outlining ways Alberta could push back against the federal hate crime law.
stories.detail: EDMONTON - Alberta's government is taking a symbolic stand against Ottawa's decision to remove religious speech as a defence to hate crimes, although it acknowledges it already gets final say on whether many cases get prosecuted.

details.summary: The UCP government is expected to invoke the sovereignty act in the legislature and table a motion outlining ways Alberta could push back against the federal hate crime law.

EDMONTON - Alberta's government is taking a symbolic stand against Ottawa's decision to remove religious speech as a defence to hate crimes, although it acknowledges it already gets final say on whether many cases get prosecuted.
Alberta’s government is planning to introduce a motion under the province’s Sovereignty Act targeting the federal government’s recent anti-hate legislation.

stories.title: Kilmar Ábrego García arrives in Spain, ending Trump deportation battle
stories.summary: Ábrego García's deportation to El Salvador and return to the US became a flashpoint in the debate over President Donald Trump's immigration agenda.
stories.detail: Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for Spain Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain. A source close to Ábrego said Madrid was his first stop but that it would not be his final destination.

stories.title: Ford calls ads from gambling market he opened ‘out of control’
stories.summary: The proliferation of online gambling ads was sparked by the Ford government allowing non-government online gambling companies to enter the market in 2022.

details.summary: The proliferation of online gambling ads was sparked by the Ford government allowing non-government online gambling companies to enter the market in 2022.
The premier says he's eyeing a crackdown on "out of control" advertising amid rising concerns about the heavy toll internet gaming is taking.

stories.title: Doug Ford praises Olivia Chow for using ‘strong mayor’ powers
stories.summary: Mayor Olivia Chow's decision to use the powers she once denounced as 'not democratic' is being met with mixed reviews at Queen's Park.
